silver_dust.name: Silver Dust
silver_dust.lore: Filings of pure silver ground fine as flour and folded into a twist of oiled paper. Rubbed into a blade with a thumb of tallow, it makes plain iron bite the way a silver weapon does, until the blows wear it off. The story goes that the man who killed the Beast of Gevaudan had his bullets cast from silver; a hunter who cannot afford a silver blade makes do with this, and the dead and the shapechangers cannot tell the difference.

frost_salts.name: Frost Salts
frost_salts.lore: Pale blue crystals that frost the inside of their jar. The alchemists learned that saltpetre stirred into water steals its heat, and these do the same to anything they touch. Rubbed on a blade, they leave it furred with rime that bites like a winter wind, and a wound they touch goes stiff and slow. The fire-born of the deep cannot bear them.

viper_venom.name: Viper Venom
viper_venom.lore: A stoppered vial of yellow-green venom milked from the fangs of an adder. Heracles dipped his arrows in the Hydra's blood and every scratch they gave was death. This is a humbler poison, but painted along an edge it turns each cut into a wound that keeps hurting. It does nothing at all to what has no blood to poison: the dead, the stone and the things that live on venom themselves.

flask_of_holy_water.name: Flask of Holy Water
flask_of_holy_water.lore: Water blessed at a wayside shrine and stoppered in a thick clay flask made to break. Sprinkled on a blade it makes every blow a blessed one, and dashed against the dead or the damned it burns them like lamp oil. To a wolf or a man it is only water. Pilgrims carried it down into the dark for exactly that reason.

water_of_siloam.name: Water of Siloam
water_of_siloam.lore: Water drawn from the Pool of Siloam below Jerusalem, where a man born blind washed the mud from his eyes and saw. The flask is sealed with wax and a little cross of lead. It hits the unholy far harder than shrine water does, and its blessing lasts longer on a blade. To anything that is not cursed or damned it does nothing at all.

water_of_life.name: Water of Life
water_of_life.lore: John saw a river of the water of life, clear as crystal, flowing from the throne of God. This crystal flask holds a mouthful of something very like it, and it glows faintly in the dark. The demons of the Abyss scream at the sight of it. A blade wet with it stays blessed through twenty blows, and a flask of it broken on a fiend is a terrible thing to see.

flask_of_fire_oil.name: Flask of Fire Oil
flask_of_fire_oil.lore: A clay flask of thick lamp oil with a rag stuffed in its neck. Light the rag and throw it, and the flask bursts into clinging flame; smear the oil along a blade and light it, and the blade burns for a dozen blows. Beasts and trolls are afraid of fire, and a troll cannot close a burn the way it closes a cut.

greek_fire.name: Greek Fire
greek_fire.lore: The fire the Byzantines poured on the Arab fleets before Constantinople in the 670s. Water would not put it out, and the recipe was so secret that it was lost with the empire. This flask holds something close to it: dark, sticky and smelling of pitch and quicklime. It burns on wet stone, and it keeps burning.

medeas_fire.name: Medea's Fire
medeas_fire.lore: When Jason left her, the witch Medea sent his new bride a golden robe as a wedding gift. When the bride put it on, it burst into a fire that nothing could put out. This is the poison she steeped it in, sealed in a flask of black glass. It catches as soon as the air touches it.

hydras_blood.name: Hydra's Blood
hydras_blood.lore: When Heracles had burned the last of the Lernaean Hydra's heads, he cut the body open and dipped his arrows in its gall. Nothing it touched ever healed. One of those arrows fell on the foot of Chiron, the wise centaur who could not die, and the pain was so great that he gave his immortality away to be rid of it. Years later the centaur Nessus died of another, and his poisoned blood killed Heracles himself. This vial is dark green and oily, sealed with lead. Painted along an edge, it turns every cut into a wound that will not close. Like any venom, it does nothing to what has no blood.

flask_of_acid.name: Flask of Acid
flask_of_acid.lore: Oil of vitriol, the alchemists called it: a clear, heavy liquid in a stoppered glass flask that smokes when the stopper comes out. It eats cloth, leather and skin, and it pits a hide or a carapace so the next blows go deeper. It would eat a blade too, so nobody sensible puts it on one. Trolls hate it as they hate fire: their flesh cannot close an acid burn.

aqua_regia.name: Aqua Regia
aqua_regia.lore: Royal water: nitric and salt acids mixed, the only thing the alchemists knew that would dissolve gold, the king of metals. In 1940 a chemist in Copenhagen dissolved two Nobel medals in it so the Nazis could not take them, and after the war the gold was drawn back out of the acid and the medals were struck again. It does the same to scales and plate.

alkahest.name: Alkahest
alkahest.lore: Paracelsus dreamed of the alkahest, the universal solvent that would dissolve anything at all. His critics asked what flask could hold it. This one is cut from a single piece of rock crystal, and the liquid inside clings to the walls as if it wants out. Broken on anything, it eats it.

seed_handful.name: Handful of Seed
seed_handful.lore: A cloth twist of millet and poppy seed. In the Balkans and across the Slavic lands mourners scattered seed on a new grave and along the road home, for a vampire that rises must stop and count every grain before it can go on, and dawn comes first. Thrown at one of the blood-drinking dead, it holds the creature a few turns while it counts. Each creature counts it once; after that it knows the trick.

upas_latex.name: Upas Latex
upas_latex.lore: A stoppered gourd of the milky sap of the upas tree of Java, the ipoh poison that island hunters smeared on their blowgun darts. The London Magazine once claimed the tree killed every living thing for fifteen miles; the truth is smaller and still deadly. Worked into an edge, it turns each cut into a poisoned one. It does nothing to what has no blood.

eitr_venom.name: Vial of Eitr
eitr_venom.lore: A thick black-green venom in a vial of rime-crusted glass, so cold it smokes. Snorri says the eitr flowed out of Niflheim in the poisonous rivers of the beginning and hardened like slag; a little never hardened. Painted along a blade it is the worst poison there is, and nothing with blood in it shrugs it off for long.
